toldy_1855.citation: Ferenc Toldy, Alexandriai szent Katalin verses legendája, Pest, 1855, introduction pp. IX and XIII, footnotes.
toldy_1855.access: Previously accessible web-reader text, revisited; neither medieval manuscript nor original Szilágyi account inspected.
toldy_1855.assertion: The introduction describes a Sziget breviary written in 1399 and cites Szilágyi on Máramarossziget. The p. XIII footnote attributes a selected Catherine verse with the virgo/beata and vaga wording to the Sziget breviary after Szilágyi.
toldy_1855.limit: The named place is evidence of a historic association, not of the book's medieval place of production. The printed transcription is a mediated report.

gabriel_1942.citation: Asztrik Gábriel, ‘A debreceni könyvtár középkori kéziratai’, Magyar Könyvszemle 66 (1942), approximately pp. 362–363; opening pagination note near p. 347.
gabriel_1942.access: Web-reader text of introduction, historic collection context, and no. 167 description. No original manuscript or image examined.
gabriel_1942.assertion: The 1942 article describes a 14th-century breviary no. 167 deposited from the Máramarossziget Lyceum at the Debrecen library; a reported colophon on f. 313 says it was completed in 1399.
gabriel_1942.limit: The passage does not quote the Catherine wording or explicitly identify the book with Toldy's source. The article warns that its foliation is often private and subject to correction; f. 313 must not be assumed a modern folio. Historic custody and no. 167 are not verified current references.

almanac_1861.assertion: The academy almanac lists the Szilágyi wall-painting article under 1851, while Toldy's footnote cites 1850.
almanac_1861.limit: The publication-year discrepancy and the actual 1850/1851 source text remain unresolved.
